nodes.action: skipped the flaky tests to make CI green
the regression reached every user and forced a full rollback
ran the full regression suite before release
added a feature-flag rollback switch to limit exposure if one slipped through
pointed DNS at the new cluster before it was ready
traffic hit a cluster that could not serve it
waited for the cluster health check before switching DNS
traffic moved over without a hitch
switched to parallel execution with a fast critical path since the full suite was too slow

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Morning, Nate. Quick heads-up — I skipped the flaky tests in the CI pipeline to get it green for the release. They were timing out on the staging box, and I didn't want to block the deploy.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Uh, okay. But those flaky tests were covering the payment retry logic. You sure that's safe?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I know, I know. But we had a hard deadline, and the failures were all network timeouts, not assertion failures. I'll run them manually after the deploy.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Alright, but if something slips through, it's on you. Anyway, what's the status on the cluster migration?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: That's actually what I wanted to talk about. I pointed DNS at the new cluster before it was ready — I thought the health checks would pass, but they didn't. So traffic hit a cluster that could not serve it.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Wait, what? Did we have an outage?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Yeah, for about four minutes. I rolled back DNS immediately, but it was messy. I should have waited for the cluster health check before switching DNS. Lesson learned.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: At least you caught it fast. But that's exactly the kind of thing the regression suite is supposed to catch. Did you run the full suite before release?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I did run the full regression suite before release — it passed. But the flaky tests I skipped? One of them would have caught a race condition in the retry logic. That regression slipped into production, and it reached every user. We had to do a full rollback.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Ouch. So the full suite wasn't enough because you skipped part of it.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Exactly. But the good news is, after the rollback, I ran the full suite again — including the flaky ones — and we caught two more regressions before shipping. So at least that part worked.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: So what's the plan going forward? We can't keep skipping tests.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I'm adding a feature-flag rollback switch to the payment service. That way, if something slips through, we can disable the new path instantly without a full rollback. Limits exposure.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Good. Let's hope we don't need it.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hey, Melanie. How's the feature-flag switch working out?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: It's in place. We tested it in staging — flipped the flag off, traffic went to the old path, no hiccups. But I'm still nervous about the flaky tests.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Did you ever figure out why they were flaky?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Partially. It's a shared database in the test environment — parallel runs cause lock contention. I've been running them serially now, but it takes forever.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: So what did you do for the last release? Did you run the full suite?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Yes, I ran the full regression suite before release — all of it, no skips. And we caught two regressions before shipping. That felt good.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Nice. And the DNS migration? Did you wait for the health check this time?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I did. I waited for the cluster health check before switching DNS, and traffic moved over without a hitch. Zero downtime.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: See? Patience pays off. So we're in good shape now?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I think so. The flag gives us a safety net, and the full suite is green. I'm cautiously optimistic.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Good. Let's keep it that way.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Morning. I heard we had a near-miss in production last night?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Yeah. A regression slipped through — the full regression suite passed, but it was too slow to run on every commit, so we only ran it right before release. Turns out that wasn't enough.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: What happened exactly?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: A change to the auth service introduced a subtle bug that only showed up under high concurrency. The full suite caught it, but only after we'd already deployed. The feature flag saved us — we flipped it off in two minutes, so no user impact.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: So the flag worked. But you're saying the full suite approach was wrong?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I was wrong about relying on the full suite as the gate. It's comprehensive, but it takes 45 minutes. So we only run it at release time, and that leaves a gap for anything merged in between.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: So what are you doing instead?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: We replaced the full-suite-only approach with parallel execution and a fast critical path. I split the tests into two tiers: a critical path that runs in under 5 minutes on every merge, and the rest of the suite that runs in parallel on a bigger runner.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: And the critical path covers the high-risk stuff?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Exactly — auth, payments, checkout, anything that touches user data. The full suite still runs before release, but now we catch regressions at merge time, not release time. That's the real fix.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Makes sense. So the old approach — full suite only — fell short because it was too slow to be practical.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Right. It wasn't enough. The parallel critical path is what we needed all along.
